segments: the heirs and inheritors of paganism,
which in this world used to be celebrated.
For fortunate is he who bears the burden in firm hope for the sake of paganism.
Who inhabited the inhabited earth and settled cities,
except the good men and kings of paganism? Who established ports and rivers? Who revealed hidden sciences? To whom was the divinity revealed, giving oracles and teaching future things,
except to the renowned among the pagans? They revealed all these things,
and brought forth the healing of souls and showed their redemption,
and also brought forth the healing of bodies,
and filled the world with the uprightness of conduct
and wisdom, which is the chief of virtue.
Without these things of paganism,
the world would have been desolate and destitute,
and a great misery would have enveloped it."
These things we have quoted from the words of this man,
to show his eloquence in the Syriac tongue;
for also in Greek and Arabic his speech was exceedingly polished.
And in the year 285
(285 of the Arabs), a violent wind blew in the region of Kufa,
and it turned black.
And a heavy rain came,
and there were mighty crashes of thunder and terrible lightnings,
and black and white stones fell from the sky.
Now it was the eve of Sunday.
And in Basra again, there came hail, a single piece weighing one hundred and fifty zuz {drachmas}.
And the Arab raiders also went out against a multitude of Roman ships,
and they burned them all, together with their crews, with fire.
It is said
that there were three thousand souls in them.
And in the year 287
(287 of the Arabs), Wasif the eunuch, commander-in-chief of the Arabs in the region of Cilicia, rebelled,
and he prepared to flee by sea.
And because of this al-Mu'tadid commanded,
and burned all the ships of the Arabs.
And since it was in them that the Arabs of Tarsus used to raid by sea,
this greatly helped the Christians.
And a year later,
a severe plague occurred in the cities of Azerbaijan,
so that the living were not even able to bury the dead,
because they too were hastening swiftly along the same path of destruction.
And in this same year, Muhammad, commander-in-chief of the Arabs, invaded the land of the Romans,
and took some villages captive,
and captured one hundred warrior men,
and sixty of the clergy, priests and deacons;
